subject: Incident notification & DPA language — timelines, scope, cooperation
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on incident notice language in DPA

Hi Monica,

We are reviewing the DPA redline you shared and have a few outstanding questions specific to the incident notification and cooperation clauses before legal/procurement will sign. High level: what timing thresholds do you propose for notice (e.g., 24/48/72 hours), how are "reportable events" defined (unauthorized access vs. suspected vulnerability), and what level of support will Redwood provide for forensic artifacts and downstream notifications?

A couple of practical items:
- If there is confirmed exfiltration of PHI or PII, Procurement expects notification within 24 hours.
- We need clarity on any limits to cooperation (e.g., what you can provide if third-party subprocessors are involved).
- Are there any cross-border transfer constraints in your proposed language, and will you commit to SCCs / equivalent safeguards for EU data?

Please loop in your security and legal contacts — we can aim to finalize this this week. Attachment: SOC2_Audit_Summary.pdf (stub).

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Senior Security & Privacy Manager
NovaHealth Systems

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (Legal) and Vivek (Security) so we can propose concrete text. Quick answers up front: Redwood's baseline is 48 hours for confirmed incidents affecting customer data, with an accelerated 24-hour window for confirmed exfiltration of sensitive data (PHI/PII). We also provide forensic artifacts and a named point of contact for coordination.

We'll send a redline proposal in this thread and mark any items that we think need an exception or alternative wording. Attaching DPA_v3_redline.pdf (stub) for visibility.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novahealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed DPA language — incident notice & cooperation (redline summary)

Alicia / Monica / team,

Per Monica's note, here's the redline summary and proposed contract language we recommend including in the DPA. This is intended to balance operational responsiveness with forensic and legal constraints. We can insert verbatim into the DPA or provide as an addendum.

1) Notification timing
- Redwood will provide initial notification to Customer without undue delay and in any event within 48 hours after Redwood confirms an Incident affecting Customer Data.
- For Incidents involving confirmed unauthorized exfiltration of Sensitive Personal Data (including PHI and high-risk PII), Redwood will provide initial notification within 24 hours of confirmation.

2) Scope / definition of Incident
- "Incident" means any confirmed security event that results in unauthorized access to, acquisition of, or disclosure of Customer Data. Suspected incidents that are not confirmed will be investigated and Customer will be informed of status updates as available.

3) Content of notice and follow-up
- Initial notice will include: date/time of detection, description of nature and scope (systems, data categories), known impact, and remediation/mitigation steps taken to date.
- Redwood will provide a formal incident report within 10 business days with findings, root cause analysis (if available), remedial steps, and evidence artifacts where permissible (logs, timelines, hashes).

4) Cooperation and evidence preservation
- Redwood will provide a named technical liaison and reasonable assistance to Customer's forensic provider, including time-limited access to logs, exportable artifacts, and summary reports. Redwood will preserve relevant logs and artifacts for 90 days after an Incident unless otherwise required by law.
- Redwood reserves the right to redact or withhold specific information to comply with law enforcement requests, privileged information, or to protect third-party confidential information, and will notify Customer when such redactions occur.

5) Law enforcement and regulatory delays
- If Redwood's ability to notify or provide specific materials is delayed by a law enforcement or regulatory directive, Redwood will notify Customer of the delay and provide the materials as soon as permitted.

6) Subprocessors and transfers
- Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors upon request and will give Customer at least 30 days' notice of any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data.
- For EU transfers, Redwood will rely on SCCs and other appropriate safeguards; where necessary Redwood will execute reasonable data transfer agreements and cooperate on compliance assessments.

If this looks broadly acceptable, we can convert the summary into redline text. Open to Alicia's counter-proposals (e.g., shortening timelines).

—Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novahealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA language — incident notice & cooperation (redline summary)

Thanks Rishi — this is helpful and aligns with many of our expectations. A couple of specific asks from NovaHealth:
- For confirmed exfiltration of PHI/PII we need 24-hour notice (your language says 24 hours for confirmed exfiltration — can you confirm this will be in the contract without caveats such as "unless legally restricted" except in cases of law enforcement directions).
- Can Redwood commit to preserving artifacts for 180 days for high-severity incidents instead of 90? Our incident response team often needs additional time for cross-system correlation.
- Regarding subprocessors, Procurement would like a statement that NovaHealth can object to a new subprocessor within 15 days of notice, and if an objection is not resolved Redwood will stop processing the customer's data with that subprocessor for NovaHealth-specific data.

One more: will Redwood support template communications for notifying affected data subjects (we can redact specifics)? Procurement expects some hand-holding for the first party notification.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alicia

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novahealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA language — incident notice & cooperation (redline summary)

Alicia — thanks for the clear counterpoints. Quick responses:
- 24-hour notice for confirmed PHI/PII exfiltration: Redwood will accept contract language committing to 24-hour notification for confirmed exfiltration, except where a law enforcement or regulatory directive expressly prohibits timely disclosure; in such cases Redwood will notify you of the directive as soon as permitted. We'll keep that exception narrow and specific.
- Artifact preservation: Redwood can extend preservation to 180 days for incidents classified as "High" severity. We'll define severity with a short rubric in the DPA (high = confirmed exfiltration of Sensitive Personal Data or disruption of production customer data affecting availability).
- Subprocessor objections: We'll propose 15 days for Customer to object to a new subprocessor notice. If objection is raised and cannot be resolved, Redwood will offer alternatives (e.g., isolation of Customer's data, transition plan) or cease using that subprocessor for the Customer's data. We will try to avoid wholesale stopping of processing that would unduly interrupt service; operational detail can go in an addendum.
- Data subject notification: Redwood will provide templates and reasonable support (drafts, timelines, technical details) but final determination and obligations to notify data subjects remain Customer's responsibility.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_Revised_20260311.pdf (redline and proposed contract text). If you confirm these points, I'll circulate a final redline for signature and send a DocuSign envelope for the DPA + SOW.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
